plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch-adjusted design
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 kidney samples (6 treated, 6 control) from salmon raw counts, processed in two known batches balanced across condition. QC first checks that batch does not dominate sample structure despite being balanced. DESeq2 models ~batch + condition, using batch as a covariate since it is balanced (every batch holds both conditions) rather than confounded, per grounded guidance. edgeR quasi-likelihood is run in parallel on the same design as the required robustness check for n=6/group, and the intersection of the two gene sets is the reported high-confidence DE set. apeglm shrinks the condition log2FC for ranking/plotting; BH-FDR with independent filtering at alpha=0.05 selects significance. Because the enrichment_input here is a discrete significant-gene list (not the full ranked list — the analysis question is 'which genes differ', a gene-list-centric framing), the knowledge service's binding rule for this situation permits only over-representation analysis with an explicit universe, using the tested genes as background; this is applied against the MSigDB Hallmark human collection staged in the reference store, with the same tested-gene universe and 15-500 size window. Enrichment is explicitly flagged as descriptive/hypothesis-generating if the significant gene list is short (<50 genes, per rule R-0103), since ORA on a short list has poor power. Final report consolidates DE tables (both methods + intersection), diagnostic plots, enrichment results, and a full reproducibility record.

fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
DE + enrichment report with diagnostics and reproducibility record
fgsea preranked GSEA (rank_metric=stat) on MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome as second collection
GO over-representation (enrichGO, BP) with rrvgo semantic-similarity term reduction, universe = tested genes, on the significant gene list (padj<0.05)
Over-representation analysis with an explicit universe (MSigDB Hallmark gene sets; universe = tested genes)
